result:
The digest runs as a job over existing notification records. There are two normal entry points:

1. On a Node.js server, `register()` in [src/instrumentation.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/be81574e-76c6-4d2b-83e8-97ab364e2847/src/instrumentation.ts) registers event handlers and starts the in-process scheduler. In [src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/be81574e-76c6-4d2b-83e8-97ab364e2847/src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts), `tick()` runs every minute and enqueues `digest-email` at a 60-minute cadence. `drain()` and `runHandler()` in [src/server/jobs/queue.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/be81574e-76c6-4d2b-83e8-97ab364e2847/src/server/jobs/queue.ts) dispatch it to `runDigestEmailJob(new Date())`.
2. An external scheduler can POST to [src/app/api/cron/digest/route.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/be81574e-76c6-4d2b-83e8-97ab364e2847/src/app/api/cron/digest/route.ts). `POST()` first checks the `x-taskflow-cron` header against `TASKFLOW_CRON_SECRET` via `assertCronSecret()`, then calls the same job with the current time.

There is also a `digest.due` event bridge in `registerDigestBridge()` in [src/server/services/event-registry.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/be81574e-76c6-4d2b-83e8-97ab364e2847/src/server/services/event-registry.ts). It enqueues the same job if that event is emitted. The queue handler runs the organization-wide job and does not use the event’s recipient or window payload; the application code contains no emitter for this event.

`runDigestEmailJob()` in [src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/be81574e-76c6-4d2b-83e8-97ab364e2847/src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts) gets up to 50 organization IDs from `listOrgIdsForRollup()` in [src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/be81574e-76c6-4d2b-83e8-97ab364e2847/src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts). That query reads organizations with usage rows, ordered by oldest measurement; the digest job does not paginate beyond that batch. It loads each organization and calls `shouldRunForOrg()`, which rejects archived organizations and requires the current UTC hour to equal `org.settings.digestHourUtc`. The job also checks `digest_email` with `isEnabled()` and `buildFlagContext()`. In [src/config/feature-flags.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/be81574e-76c6-4d2b-83e8-97ab364e2847/src/config/feature-flags.ts), that flag requires Growth or a higher plan, unless an organization-level override enables it.

For each eligible organization, `listDigestRecipients()` in [src/server/services/digest-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/be81574e-76c6-4d2b-83e8-97ab364e2847/src/server/services/digest-service.ts) calls `listDigestSubscribers()` in [src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/be81574e-76c6-4d2b-83e8-97ab364e2847/src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts). The query returns distinct user IDs with at least one preference row in that organization where `digestOnly` is true. It does not require that row’s `email` or `inApp` setting to be true. `updateNotificationPreferenceAction()` in [src/actions/notifications/update-preferences.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/be81574e-76c6-4d2b-83e8-97ab364e2847/src/actions/notifications/update-preferences.ts) checks the feature flag when someone enables that preference.

The content originates earlier, when events occur. `registerFanOut()` in [src/server/services/notification-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/be81574e-76c6-4d2b-83e8-97ab364e2847/src/server/services/notification-service.ts) subscribes to assignment, overdue issue, comment and member-joined events and calls `notify()` with the relevant recipients and message. `notify()` removes duplicate recipients, skips the event’s actor, consults each recipient’s per-kind preference through `resolveChannels()`, and skips recipients with no enabled channels. `insertNotifications()` in [src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/be81574e-76c6-4d2b-83e8-97ab364e2847/src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts) stores the resulting rows as unread.

For each subscriber, the job passes `buildDigest()` a window from **exactly 24 hours before the job’s `now` through `now`**, inclusive. `buildDigest()` rechecks that the organization exists and the flag is enabled, then calls `listUnreadSince()`. That query selects the person’s unread rows in the organization created at or after the start, newest first; `buildDigest()` removes rows after the end, maps each to a `DigestEntry` containing its ID, kind, title, link and creation time, and keeps at most 50. The selection is **all qualifying unread notifications**, not only kinds whose current preference is `digestOnly` or rows whose channel includes email.

If the bundle has at least one entry and the user still exists, `renderDigest()` passes the organization ID, recipient name, entry count, window and first entry’s title to `renderEmail()` in [src/server/services/email-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/be81574e-76c6-4d2b-83e8-97ab364e2847/src/server/services/email-service.ts). The current renderer makes a generic HTML table and plain-text version from those properties; it does not pass the entry list to the separate `DigestEmail` component. `sendEmail()` currently logs the recipient, subject and HTML size rather than sending through a mail transport. After that call returns, the job marks each included notification read and increments its processed count.

A subscribed person therefore gets no digest on a run if their organization is absent from the selected batch, missing, archived, outside its configured UTC hour, or no longer has the digest flag enabled. They also get none if the organization disappears during the build, the user record is missing, or there are no qualifying unread notifications in the window—for example, the person already read them, they are older than 24 hours, or the event produced no notification row for them. An error while building or rendering is caught and recorded as a failed recipient. Because successfully included entries are marked read, a repeat run normally skips them; however, the 50-entry cap and lack of a per-day send record mean a later run can still process other unread entries.
